subject: economics
title: ZIMSEC O-Level Economics

officialDocument.title: Economics Syllabus, Forms 1 - 4, 2015 - 2022 (Ministry of Primary and Secondary Education, Curriculum Development and Technical Services), examined by ZIMSEC at O Level
officialDocument.publisher: Ministry of Primary and Secondary Education (Curriculum Development and Technical Services) / Zimbabwe School Examinations Council (ZIMSEC)

sourceNote: Topic names and their numbers (6.1 to 6.18) are transcribed from the topic list (6.0) of the Ministry's Economics Syllabus Forms 1 - 4 (2015 - 2022); the content of each topic and the form in which it is taught come from the scope and sequence (7.0) and the competency matrix (8.0). Sub-topic and objective codes are ours. Learning-objective statements are our own paraphrase; no syllabus text is reproduced.
notes: Source (read 2026-10-08): the Mashonaland West provincial education office's copy of the Ministry document, file 'Economics Forms 1-4.pdf' (http://www.mopsemashwest.gov.zw/files/Economics%20Forms%201-4.pdf; the site's https certificate has expired, so the https URL recorded here may not load), read through a text rendering. The cover prints 'Forms 1 - 4', '2015 - 2022' and the year 2015. The scope-and-sequence and competency-matrix tables come out of the text rendering with their columns scrambled; the form of each item is read from the column positions and cross-checked against the matrix (Form 1 to Form 4 sections, 8.1 to 8.4). Check every heading, the form of each item and each objective against a clean copy from ZIMSEC.
Subject code: not printed in the syllabus document. ZIMSEC O-Level Economics is commonly cited as 4048; confirm it (code left null).

Version dates: assumed first examined in November 2018 (effectiveFrom 2018-01-01), as for the other 2015-2022 files. Under the Heritage-Based Curriculum (2024-2030) new syllabi were issued; confirm which syllabus the November 2026 and later O-Level Economics examinations use, set effectiveTo, and create a new version file when a new syllabus replaces this one.

Assessment (9.0) as read: continuous assessment 30% (practical assignments, theory tests and a written research project; Form 1 5%, Form 2 5%, Form 3 10%, Form 4 10%) and a summative examination 70%: Paper 1 Multiple choice (40 four-option items, 1 hour 15 minutes, 40 marks, 20%), Paper 2 Data response (two compulsory 20-mark questions testing knowledge, understanding and problem solving, 1 hour 15 minutes, 40 marks, 20%) and Paper 3 Essays (attempt 4 of 10 questions, 40 marks, 30%). The assessment table gives Paper 3 1 hour 15 minutes but the description of papers says 2 hours: 75 minutes is recorded and must be confirmed, together with the marks per essay (40 marks over four essays suggests 10 each; ZIMSEC may set two-part essays).

Specification grid as read: Papers 1 and 3 examine all 18 topics; Paper 2 (data response) examines Production, Labour, Demand theory, Supply theory, Market equilibrium, Cost structures and revenue, Market structures, National income accounting, Inflation, Population, Unemployment and job creation, Domestic and foreign trade, and Economic growth and development. The other five topics (6.1, 6.2, 6.10, 6.12, 6.18) carry components [1, 3]. Skill distribution printed: knowledge and understanding 30 (Paper 1) and 20 (Paper 2), interpretation and application 40 and 40, problem solving 30 and 40 (percentages).

Topic 6.18 'Market failure and government intervention' is in the topic list and the specification grid but has no scope-and-sequence entry and no competency-matrix pages; its sub-topics and objectives here are ours, based on the glossary (public goods, private and social costs, ad valorem tax, privatisation). Confirm the expected depth with ZIMSEC; the concepts are shared with Cambridge 0455.

Where the topic list and the matrix place an item under different topics, the matrix is followed: fiscal and monetary policy are taught under Money and banking (Form 4), mobility of labour under Population (Form 3), division of labour under Production (Form 2). Taxation is not named in the matrix but fiscal policy and the glossary (progressive, proportional and ad valorem taxation) require it.

The matrix sometimes repeats a page (Domestic and foreign trade, Form 3; National income accounting, Form 4) and the text rendering garbles some cells (for example the public corporation and limited company cells of Form 3); nothing was inferred from garbled cells beyond the clearly legible headings.

Zimbabwe-specific items (land reform, Zimbabwe's economic system, inflation rates in Zimbabwe, unemployment trends, indigenisation, CAMPFIRE, EMA, community share trusts, ZIMASSET as a suggested resource) are taught with well-established facts only; content must not invent or quote statistics. The matrix asks learners to 'identify the current rate of inflation in Zimbabwe': content teaches how to find and interpret the official figure rather than stating one.

Not in this syllabus (taught in the family for Cambridge IGCSE only): households' spending and saving, labour- and capital-intensive production and the demand for factors, objectives of firms, government macroeconomic aims and conflicts, supply-side policy, recession, poverty, international differences in living standards, globalisation, and causes, consequences and policies for current account imbalances. The continuous assessment (projects, practical assignments) is not simulated.
overview: The ZIMSEC O-Level Economics syllabus (Forms 1-4) introduces the basic economic problem and economic systems, then microeconomics (production, labour, demand and supply, elasticity, market equilibrium, costs and revenue, market structures and business organisation) and macroeconomics (national income, money and banking, inflation, population, unemployment, trade and the balance of payments, growth and development, market failure). It is taught with Zimbabwean examples and stresses enterprise, sustainable resource use and Unhu/Ubuntu/Vumunhu.
assessmentOverview: Continuous assessment (assignments, tests and a research project, Forms 1-4) carries 30%. The examination carries 70%: Paper 1 has 40 four-option multiple-choice items (1 hour 15 minutes, 20%), Paper 2 has two compulsory 20-mark data-response questions (1 hour 15 minutes, 20%) and Paper 3 asks candidates to answer four of ten essay questions (40 marks, 30%).

components.name: Paper 1: Multiple choice
components.description: 40 compulsory multiple-choice items with four options (A to D), covering all 18 topics.

components.name: Paper 2: Data response
components.description: Two compulsory data-response questions of 20 marks each, testing knowledge, understanding and problem solving on 13 of the topics.

components.name: Paper 3: Essays
components.description: Ten essay questions on all the topics, of which candidates answer four. Duration printed as 1 hour 15 minutes in the assessment table and 2 hours in the description of papers (to be confirmed).

children.name: The basic economic problem and the basic economic questions

objectives.text: Form 1: explain resources, needs, wants and scarcity, and the basic economic problem of limited resources, unlimited wants and choice.
Form 2: identify and explain the questions of what, how and for whom to produce.
Form 3: explain opportunity cost and apply it to choices made by individuals, firms and government.

children.name: The production possibility curve and efficient resource allocation

objectives.text: Form 3: explain what a PPC shows and construct one from a table of output combinations.
Form 3: interpret points on, inside and outside the PPC as efficient, inefficient and unattainable, and show opportunity cost on it.

children.name: Shapes and shifts of the PPC

objectives.text: Form 4: describe concave, convex and straight-line PPCs and what each shape means.
Form 4: identify outward and inward shifts of a PPC and explain their causes.
Form 4: analyse efficient and sustainable resource allocation.
Form 3: distinguish statements of fact (positive) from statements of opinion (normative).

children.name: Types and features of economic systems

objectives.text: Form 1: explain market, planned and mixed economic systems and state the features of each.
Form 2: explain how each system answers the three basic economic questions.
Form 3: state and explain the advantages and disadvantages of the market economy.

children.name: Planned and mixed economies and Zimbabwe's economic system

objectives.text: Form 3: state and explain the advantages and disadvantages of planned and mixed economies.
Form 4: identify similarities and differences among the economic systems and describe Zimbabwe's current economic system.

children.name: Factors of production and their rewards

objectives.text: Form 1: explain production, list and explain the four factors of production and match each to its reward.
Form 2: explain the rewards to the factors of production.

children.name: Stages of production, value addition and direct and indirect production

objectives.text: Form 2: outline the primary, secondary and tertiary stages of production with examples of activities in each.
Form 3: describe how the three stages depend on each other and explain value addition and its importance.
Form 3: distinguish direct from indirect production.
Form 2: state the advantages and disadvantages of specialisation and division of labour.
Form 3: explain land reform, identify the aims of Zimbabwe's land reform programme and outline its economic effects.
Form 4: describe and calculate productivity (total, average and marginal product) and describe ways of improving it.
Form 4: explain the factors affecting the location of industry and how and why government influences location.

children.name: Labour, types of workers and employees' interests

objectives.text: Form 1: explain labour and its reward, and list employees' interests in employment (wages, security, health and safety, fringe benefits).
Form 1: identify and describe unskilled, semi-skilled and skilled workers.

children.name: Employers' and employees' associations; trade unions and government

objectives.text: Form 2: identify employers' associations and employees' associations (trade unions, workers' committees) and explain their roles.
Form 3: describe the role of trade unions and explain government intervention in wage determination.

children.name: Demand for and supply of labour; wage determination

objectives.text: Form 3: explain derived demand for labour and the factors affecting the demand for and supply of labour.
Form 4: explain how wages are determined in labour markets.
Form 4: identify and explain the bases of wage differentials (training, risk, prestige, gender, government policy, culture).

children.name: Demand, the law of demand and the demand curve

objectives.text: Form 1: explain effective demand, outline the law of demand and show the relationship between price and quantity demanded.
Form 2: tabulate a demand schedule, plot a demand curve and distinguish effective from latent demand.

children.name: Determinants of demand and changes in demand

objectives.text: Form 3: identify the determinants of demand and distinguish a change in demand from a change in quantity demanded, illustrating each.
Form 4: explain and calculate price elasticity of demand, interpret its value and illustrate the degrees of elasticity.
Form 4: outline the determinants of elasticity of demand.
Form 4: explain the importance of elasticity of demand to households, firms and government, including the effect of price changes on revenue.

children.name: Income and cross elasticity of demand

objectives.text: Form 4: calculate and interpret income and cross elasticity of demand.

children.name: Supply, the law of supply and the supply curve

objectives.text: Form 1: explain supply, describe the law of supply and show the relationship between price and quantity supplied.
Form 2: draw a supply curve and describe the price-supply relationship it shows.

children.name: Determinants of supply and changes in supply

objectives.text: Form 2: outline the determinants of supply.
Form 3: show how the determinants shift the supply curve and distinguish increases and decreases in supply from extensions and contractions.
Form 3: explain climate change, outline its effects on production and suggest mitigating measures.
Form 4: explain and calculate price elasticity of supply, interpret its value, describe its determinants and its significance in real situations.
Form 2: describe how buyers and sellers interact in a market and how prices allocate resources.

children.name: Interaction of demand and supply; equilibrium

objectives.text: Form 2: illustrate the interaction of demand and supply and explain equilibrium price, quantity and point.
Form 3: show shifts of the demand and supply curves, how a new equilibrium is established and what causes the shifts.
Form 4: explain price ceilings and price floors and illustrate their effects (shortages and surpluses).
Form 1: explain and calculate fixed, variable and total costs.
Form 2: explain semi-variable costs and illustrate the cost curves.
Form 3: distinguish the short run from the long run and illustrate average cost curves.
Form 1 and Form 4: explain and calculate total, average and marginal revenue.

children.name: Marginal cost, profit maximisation and efficiency

objectives.text: Form 4: explain marginal cost and identify the profit-maximising rule (MR = MC).
Form 4: describe normal and abnormal profit, the break-even condition (AR = AC) and economic efficiency.
Form 3: describe the features of perfect competition and explain its advantages and disadvantages.
Form 3: describe the features of monopolistic competition and explain its advantages and disadvantages.
Form 3: describe the features of monopoly and explain its advantages and disadvantages.

children.name: Short-run and long-run equilibrium; comparing market structures

objectives.text: Form 4: describe short-run and long-run equilibrium in each market structure and identify the profit-maximising output.
Form 4: compare the features and outcomes of the different market structures.

children.name: Sole traders, partnerships, co-operatives and limited companies

objectives.text: Form 1: describe sole traders and partnerships and outline their features, advantages and disadvantages.
Form 2: describe co-operatives and their advantages and disadvantages.
Form 2: explain limited companies and outline the documents used to set them up and their contents.
Form 3: compare private and public limited companies and outline their advantages and disadvantages.
Form 3: describe public corporations and their advantages and disadvantages.
Form 3: describe the features of multinational companies and outline their costs and benefits to host countries.
Form 4: describe methods of raising finance such as shares, debentures and leasing.
Form 4: explain methods of growth of firms and describe the effects of vertical and horizontal integration on stakeholders.
Form 4: distinguish between economies and diseconomies of scale.

children.name: Small to medium enterprises and business plans

objectives.text: Form 4: outline the features of SMEs and describe how they survive.
Form 4: draw up a business plan with a cash-flow projection.

children.name: GDP, GNP and the measurement of national income

objectives.text: Form 1: explain Gross Domestic Product and Gross National Product.
Form 2: identify and explain the income, output and expenditure methods.
Form 3: identify and explain the components of national income (consumption, government expenditure, investment, exports and imports).

children.name: Uses and limitations of national income statistics

objectives.text: Form 4: discuss the uses of national income statistics by different agents and explain their limitations.
Form 1: explain barter trade and its advantages and disadvantages, and outline the types of money (M1, M2 and M3).
Form 2: outline the characteristics of money and explain its functions.

children.name: Financial institutions and the central bank

objectives.text: Form 3: describe the role of commercial banks, merchant banks and building societies in an economy.
Form 3: explain the functions of a central bank, using the Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe.

children.name: Fiscal policy and the national budget

objectives.text: Form 4: describe how fiscal policy (government spending and the national budget) can be used to achieve economic objectives.
Form 4: explain taxation as a fiscal policy instrument (direct and indirect, progressive and proportional taxes).
Form 4: distinguish monetary from fiscal policy and describe how monetary policy can be used to achieve economic objectives.
Form 2: explain inflation and describe and distinguish demand-pull and cost-push inflation.
Form 4: calculate the rate of inflation using the CPI and RPI and compare rates of inflation in Zimbabwe for different periods.

children.name: Effects of inflation and policies to curb it

objectives.text: Form 3: explain the effects of inflation on consumers, producers, government and the functions of money.
Form 4: explain the monetary and fiscal policy tools used to curb inflation.
Form 1: explain population and the census and discuss why a census is conducted.
Form 2: describe the geographical, occupational and demographic distribution of population and explain population growth.
Form 3: explain the factors affecting population (birth rates, death rates, migration, government policy).
Form 2: identify high, low and sustainable population sizes and discuss their effects.
Form 3: discuss how population size and composition affect economic development.
Form 3: explain occupational and geographical mobility of labour as factors affecting population and the labour force.
Form 3: identify the causes of HIV and AIDS, explain their effects on population and economic development and suggest solutions.

children.name: Size and composition of the labour force

objectives.text: Form 4: relate the composition of the population to the labour force and explain what affects its size and composition.
Form 4: describe ways of controlling population.
Form 1: explain unemployment and the labour force and distinguish the employed from the unemployed.
Form 2: identify and explain structural, frictional, seasonal, regional and cyclical unemployment.

children.name: Effects of and solutions to unemployment

objectives.text: Form 3: outline the effects of unemployment and propose solutions.

children.name: Unemployment trends and job creation in Zimbabwe

objectives.text: Form 4: describe unemployment trends in Zimbabwe and job creation.
Form 4: explain how enterprise and indigenisation can reduce unemployment and plan a small income-generating project.
Form 1: describe the characteristics and importance of domestic trade and of retailers and wholesalers.
Form 1: distinguish formal from informal trade and state the role of informal traders.
Form 2: describe and compare home and foreign trade and outline the advantages and disadvantages of international trade.
Form 3: distinguish exports from imports and explain the reasons for international trade: absolute advantage, comparative advantage and factor endowment.

children.name: Balance of trade and balance of payments

objectives.text: Form 3: calculate the balance of trade and the current account of the balance of payments and interpret a deficit or surplus.
Form 4: describe, calculate and interpret the terms of trade.
Form 4: explain foreign exchange and exchange rates and the relationship between the Zimbabwean currency and other currencies.
Form 4: outline the problems resulting from foreign exchange shortages and the possible sources of foreign currency.
Form 4: outline the reasons for and the merits and demerits of free trade.
Form 4: describe ways of protectionism, with their merits and demerits.
Form 4: give reasons for economic integration, with SADC, COMESA and the African Union as examples.
Form 1: explain economic growth and identify signs of growth.
Form 3: identify and explain the causes of economic growth.
Form 4: identify and discuss the costs and benefits of economic growth.
Form 2: explain economic development and identify signs of development.
Form 3: distinguish economic growth from development and explain the causes of development.
Form 4: state and explain the indicators of growth and development.
Form 4: explain sustainable resource management and how economic agents should manage resources sustainably.
Form 4: explain sustainable development, discuss ways of achieving it and plan a sustainable development project.

topics.name: Market failure and government intervention
topics.description: Listed in the topic list (6.18) and in the Paper 1 and Paper 3 content of the specification grid, but the scope and sequence and the competency matrix give it no content. The sub-topics are ours, taken from the glossary terms (public goods, private and social costs and benefits, ad valorem tax, privatisation, market failure).

children.name: Market failure: public, merit and demerit goods

objectives.text: Explain market failure and why markets fail to provide public goods and under-provide merit goods.

children.name: Private, external and social costs and benefits

objectives.text: Distinguish private, external and social costs and benefits and explain their effect on resource allocation.
Explain how indirect taxes and subsidies are used to correct market failure.
Explain regulation, privatisation, nationalisation and direct provision as forms of government intervention.
